insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl has cryptographically confirmed $4.93M in GMV across 103,038 receipts — deterministic proof of purchase, not inferred intent. For brands paying $5+ CPM to reach people who might buy, this represents a structurally different signal class.

Walmart (298 receipts), Kroger (132), Target (124), and Costco (119) account for the dominant share of verified 14-day purchase activity, with grocery-supermarkets leading all categories at 1,213 receipts and $52,293 in confirmed GMV. Brands in CPG and household goods have a direct line to verified buyers at the exact retailers where shelf competition plays out.

Category entropy has held at 2.905 bits and store entropy at 3.115 bits across multiple consecutive snapshots — no category rotation, no single-retailer distortion. Throughput changes are broad-based, meaning the signal composition is consistent enough to build targeting logic against.

Pre-rolloff 7-day GMV peaked near $83.5K for two consecutive cycles, then stepped down to $74,994 in the most recent cycle — a ~10% drop that may indicate a throughput ceiling forming around the $83–84K weekly range. The next pre-rolloff reading (~2026-11-13T20:15) is the critical test; brands evaluating scale should monitor whether weekly verified volume stabilizes or continues contracting.

Restaurants/dining (843 receipts, $25,363), retail/department stores (665 receipts, $27,609), gas/convenience (450 receipts, $19,807), and The UPS Store (43 receipts, re-entered visibility) confirm that verified purchase data extends well beyond grocery — relevant for QSR, fuel, and logistics-adjacent brands seeking cookieless audience validation.

insights.topic: Geographic pulse cells and coverage durability
insights.insight: Of 19 active CBSAs, at least three are classified as recurring pulse cells — appearing intermittently rather than continuously — which means geographic targeting built on this data requires freshness discipline; metro coverage is real but not yet uniformly durable across all markets.
